comment: Budget conformance fixture (SPEC.md 7.7, 19.3). Pins the bytes where two independent implementations drift: the budget block's shape and canonical serialization under the envelope signature, the refusal detail field names, the pause shape, revision ordering, and the deadline skew boundary. Both SDKs implement this as of 2026-07-27. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY: when a test against it fails, fix the implementation, and when the fixture itself is believed wrong, change it only with a spec change alongside.

identities.comment: The same published test vectors inbound-protections.json uses, deliberately: they are not real identities and control nothing, and reusing them keeps any new private-key-shaped string out of the repository.

block.comment: 7.7: revision REQUIRED (integer >= 0, 0 on the initiating request); at least one of deadline / cost_ceiling present; deadline a full RFC-3339 instant (date-only invalid); amount_micro a non-negative integer (1,000,000 micro-units = one currency unit; no floats near money, ever); currency an ISO 4217 code. Absent fields are OMITTED in canonical JSON, never null.

invalid.why: deadline must be a full RFC-3339 instant
absent is omitted, never null - null deadline is malformed

envelope.comment: A fully-formed, really-signed request carrying a budget, generated by the TypeScript SDK's canonicalization and signing. 'canonical' is the canonical envelope JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace, absent fields omitted) WITHOUT the domain prefix; the signature covers signed_bytes_prefix + canonical (SPEC.md 5.3). Any conforming implementation MUST rebuild those bytes from the envelope and verify the signature; one changed micro-unit must fail verification.

input.question: controlling case law on anticipatory repudiation

revisions.comment: 7.7: absolute, never deltas - each revision states the entire budget and the highest revision is the whole truth. Strictly-greater wins: lower or equal revisions are ignored (receiver side) or refused (task manager, TASK_INVALID_TRANSITION). No retroactive violation: a revision whose deadline is already past, or whose ceiling is already below reported spend, is refused.

ordering_case.why: rev 1 arrives after rev 2 (ignored: lower); the second rev 2 is ignored (equal, first-writer wins); absolute semantics mean rev 2's block replaced rev 0's ENTIRELY

absolute_case.why: rev 1 omits deadline, so the current budget HAS NO deadline - a revision is the whole budget, nothing is inherited from rev 0

refusals.comment: 12.2 / 7.7. The refusal SHOULD carry the responder's estimate; these field names are the protocol between implementations, pinned here because the spec prose does not name them. error.details is the carrier in every case.

budget_insufficient.note: details.estimate is a cost_ceiling-shaped object: the responder's price for the work

deadline_unmeetable.note: details.earliest_completion is an RFC-3339 instant, NOT details.estimate - the two refusals carry differently-typed estimates under different names so a reader never type-sniffs

budget_exhausted_pause.note: the pause is a NON-TERMINAL respond: status input_required, error.code BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, details.spent + details.estimate_to_finish (both cost_ceiling-shaped). 'spent', not 'spend'. On a bare request this same reply carries the task_id that promotes to deferred mode (7.0).

deadline_exceeded_marker.note: a marker on late completions (task record / platform event), never a refusal an SDK sends at admission

deadline.comment: 7.7: deadlines are compared under the 22.3 clock-skew tolerance (MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_AHEAD_MS, 300000 ms), at second granularity, bounds inclusive: a deadline is past only once now exceeds deadline + tolerance by a full second.

cases.why: exactly at the tolerance bound - inclusive
one full second beyond the bound
offset forms normalize to the same instant

not_covered.comment: Boundaries, written down so nobody mistakes them for gaps.
items: Whether a responder's estimate or spend report is TRUE is unverifiable by design (7.7: honor-system spend, centrally-enforceable time). This fixture pins shapes, not honesty.
Party authorization on revisions (UNAUTHORIZED) is the task manager's check - it holds the Task's parties. SDKs enforce monotonicity and signatures only.
Settlement, payment and billing are out of scope for the specification and for this fixture.
